testCases.name: [TC-004] Remember Me — Session Persists Across Browser Restart
testCases.precondition:
Registered user account exists: `test@demo.com` / `Test1234!`
Browser has no existing session cookie for the application

steps.expectedResult: User is redirected to `/dashboard`; a persistent auth token is set in the browser (cookie `max-age` ≥ 30 days)

steps.description: Close the browser completely and reopen it

steps.expectedResult: User is still authenticated; redirected to `/dashboard` without being prompted to log in again
Token expiry is `createdAt + 30 days` (±1 minute tolerance)

testCases.outcome: User remains authenticated after a full browser restart; the auth token has a 30-day TTL and is not a session-only cookie. ---
testCases.content:
## Test Case: [TC-004] Remember Me — Session Persists Across Browser Restart

**Type:** Functional
**Priority:** High

### Preconditions
- Registered user account exists: `test@demo.com` / `Test1234!`
- Browser has no existing session cookie for the application

### Test Steps
| Step | Action | Expected Result |
|------|--------|-----------------|
| 1 | Navigate to `/login` | Login page is displayed |
| 2 | Enter valid email and password | Fields populated |
| 3 | Check the "Remember me" checkbox | Checkbox is selected |
| 4 | Click "Sign In" | User is redirected to `/dashboard`; a persistent auth token is set in the browser (cookie `max-age` ≥ 30 days) |
| 5 | Close the browser completely and reopen it | Browser starts a fresh session |
| 6 | Navigate to `/dashboard` | User is still authenticated; redirected to `/dashboard` without being prompted to log in again |
| 7 | Inspect the auth token expiry | Token expiry is `createdAt + 30 days` (±1 minute tolerance) |

### Expected Outcome
User remains authenticated after a full browser restart; the auth token has a 30-day TTL and is not a session-only cookie.

---

testCases.name: [TC-005] Remember Me — Session Does NOT Persist Without Checkbox
testCases.precondition:
Registered user account: `test@demo.com` / `Test1234!`
Browser has no existing session cookie

steps.description: Enter valid email and password; leave "Remember me" **unchecked**

steps.expectedResult: User redirected to `/dashboard`; auth token is a session cookie (no `max-age` / `expires` attribute)

steps.description: Close the browser completely and reopen it

testCases.outcome: Without "Remember me", the auth token is a session cookie that expires on browser close. ---
testCases.content:
## Test Case: [TC-005] Remember Me — Session Does NOT Persist Without Checkbox

**Type:** Functional
**Priority:** Medium

### Preconditions
- Registered user account: `test@demo.com` / `Test1234!`
- Browser has no existing session cookie

### Test Steps
| Step | Action | Expected Result |
|------|--------|-----------------|
| 1 | Navigate to `/login` | Login page displayed |
| 2 | Enter valid email and password; leave "Remember me" **unchecked** | Fields populated, checkbox unchecked |
| 3 | Click "Sign In" | User redirected to `/dashboard`; auth token is a session cookie (no `max-age` / `expires` attribute) |
| 4 | Close the browser completely and reopen it | Browser starts a fresh session |

### Expected Outcome
Without "Remember me", the auth token is a session cookie that expires on browser close.

testCases.name: [TC-006] Login with Non-Existent Email

steps.expectedResult: Error message **"Invalid email or password"** is displayed; user remains on `/login`
Response arrives in the same time window as a failed-password response (timing must not reveal whether the email exists)

testCases.outcome: The application returns the same generic error for a non-existent email as for a wrong password, preventing user enumeration. Response timing does not leak existence of the account. ---
testCases.content:
## Test Case: [TC-006] Login with Non-Existent Email

**Type:** Negative
**Priority:** High

### Preconditions
- No account registered under `notregistered@demo.com`

### Test Steps
| Step | Action | Expected Result |
|------|--------|-----------------|
| 1 | Navigate to `/login` | Login page displayed |
| 2 | Enter `notregistered@demo.com` in the email field | Field populated |
| 3 | Enter any password (e.g. `AnyPass1!`) | Field populated |
| 4 | Click "Sign In" | Error message **"Invalid email or password"** is displayed; user remains on `/login` |
| 5 | Verify response time | Response arrives in the same time window as a failed-password response (timing must not reveal whether the email exists) |

### Expected Outcome
The application returns the same generic error for a non-existent email as for a wrong password, preventing user enumeration. Response timing does not leak existence of the account.

testCases.name: [TC-007] Login Form Submission with Empty Fields

steps.description: Leave both email and password blank; click "Sign In"
steps.expectedResult: Client-side validation fires; submission is blocked; both fields are highlighted as required

steps.description: Enter a valid email only, leave password blank; click "Sign In"
steps.expectedResult: Submission blocked; password field highlighted as required

steps.description: Leave email blank, enter a password; click "Sign In"
steps.expectedResult: Submission blocked; email field highlighted as required

steps.description: Confirm no HTTP request is sent for any of the above
steps.expectedResult: Network tab shows no POST to `/api/auth/login`

testCases.outcome: The form enforces presence validation client-side; no login request reaches the backend when mandatory fields are empty. ---
testCases.content:
## Test Case: [TC-007] Login Form Submission with Empty Fields

**Type:** Negative
**Priority:** Medium

### Preconditions
- None

### Test Steps
| Step | Action | Expected Result |
|------|--------|-----------------|
| 1 | Navigate to `/login` | Login page displayed |
| 2 | Leave both email and password blank; click "Sign In" | Client-side validation fires; submission is blocked; both fields are highlighted as required |
| 3 | Enter a valid email only, leave password blank; click "Sign In" | Submission blocked; password field highlighted as required |
| 4 | Leave email blank, enter a password; click "Sign In" | Submission blocked; email field highlighted as required |
| 5 | Confirm no HTTP request is sent for any of the above | Network tab shows no POST to `/api/auth/login` |

### Expected Outcome
The form enforces presence validation client-side; no login request reaches the backend when mandatory fields are empty.

---

testCases.name: [TC-008] SQL Injection and XSS Attempts in Login Fields
testCases.precondition:
The application is deployed in a test environment with server-side logging accessible
Registered user: `test@demo.com` / `Test1234!`

steps.description: Enter `' OR '1'='1' --` in the email field; enter any password; click "Sign In"
steps.expectedResult: Response is "Invalid email or password"; user is NOT authenticated; no SQL error or stack trace exposed

steps.description: Enter `<script>alert('xss')</script>` in the email field; any password; click "Sign In"
steps.expectedResult: Script is not executed; value is escaped in any reflected output; response is the standard error message

steps.description: Enter `admin@demo.com'--` in email; any password; click "Sign In"

steps.expectedResult: No unhandled exceptions or raw SQL errors logged; all inputs are parameterised or sanitised

testCases.outcome: All injection payloads are treated as plain strings. No authentication bypass, script execution, or internal error disclosure occurs. ---
testCases.content:
## Test Case: [TC-008] SQL Injection and XSS Attempts in Login Fields

**Type:** Security
**Priority:** Critical

### Preconditions
- The application is deployed in a test environment with server-side logging accessible
- Registered user: `test@demo.com` / `Test1234!`

### Test Steps
| Step | Action | Expected Result |
|------|--------|-----------------|
| 1 | Navigate to `/login` | Login page displayed |
| 2 | Enter `' OR '1'='1' --` in the email field; enter any password; click "Sign In" | Response is "Invalid email or password"; user is NOT authenticated; no SQL error or stack trace exposed |
| 3 | Enter `<script>alert('xss')</script>` in the email field; any password; click "Sign In" | Script is not executed; value is escaped in any reflected output; response is the standard error message |
| 4 | Enter `admin@demo.com'--` in email; any password; click "Sign In" | Standard error; not authenticated |
| 5 | Check server logs | No unhandled exceptions or raw SQL errors logged; all inputs are parameterised or sanitised |

### Expected Outcome
All injection payloads are treated as plain strings. No authentication bypass, script execution, or internal error disclosure occurs.

---

testCases.name: [TC-009] Lockout Counter Resets After Successful Login
testCases.precondition:
Registered user: `test@demo.com` / `Test1234!`
No prior failed attempts on the account

steps.description: Attempt login with wrong password **4 times**
steps.expectedResult: Each attempt shows "Invalid email or password"

steps.description: Attempt login with wrong password **4 more times**
steps.expectedResult: Each attempt shows "Invalid email or password" (counter has reset to 0 after successful login)

steps.description: Attempt login with wrong password a **5th time**
steps.expectedResult: Shows "Invalid email or password" — account is NOT locked yet (counter is at 5 cumulative *since last success*, so the 6th would lock)

testCases.outcome: A successful login resets the failed-attempt counter. Prior failures before a successful login do not carry over and contribute to lockout. ---
testCases.content:
## Test Case: [TC-009] Lockout Counter Resets After Successful Login

**Type:** Edge Case
**Priority:** High

### Preconditions
- Registered user: `test@demo.com` / `Test1234!`
- No prior failed attempts on the account

### Test Steps
| Step | Action | Expected Result |
|------|--------|-----------------|
| 1 | Attempt login with wrong password **4 times** | Each attempt shows "Invalid email or password" |
| 2 | Log in with the **correct** password | User is authenticated; redirected to `/dashboard` |
| 3 | Log out | User returned to `/login` |
| 4 | Attempt login with wrong password **4 more times** | Each attempt shows "Invalid email or password" (counter has reset to 0 after successful login) |
| 5 | Attempt login with wrong password a **5th time** | Shows "Invalid email or password" — account is NOT locked yet (counter is at 5 cumulative *since last success*, so the 6th would lock) |
| 6 | Attempt login with correct credentials | User logs in successfully |

### Expected Outcome
A successful login resets the failed-attempt counter. Prior failures before a successful login do not carry over and contribute to lockout.

---

testCases.name: [TC-010] Login Response Performance — p95 Under 500ms
testCases.precondition:
Performance test tooling available (e.g. k6, JMeter, or Gatling)
Test environment is provisioned to production-equivalent spec
100 registered test user accounts available

steps.description: Configure load script: 50 concurrent virtual users, each performing a valid login over 60 seconds
Execute load test against `POST /api/auth/login` with valid credentials
Collect response time percentiles from results

steps.expectedResult: Error rate is **0%** (no 5xx responses) during the load run

testCases.outcome: At 50 concurrent users, the login endpoint responds at p95 ≤ 500ms with no server errors. ---
testCases.content:
## Test Case: [TC-010] Login Response Performance — p95 Under 500ms

**Type:** Non-Functional
**Priority:** High

### Preconditions
- Performance test tooling available (e.g. k6, JMeter, or Gatling)
- Test environment is provisioned to production-equivalent spec
- 100 registered test user accounts available

### Test Steps
| Step | Action | Expected Result |
|------|--------|-----------------|
| 1 | Configure load script: 50 concurrent virtual users, each performing a valid login over 60 seconds | Script ready |
| 2 | Execute load test against `POST /api/auth/login` with valid credentials | Requests execute |
| 3 | Collect response time percentiles from results | p50, p95, p99 captured |
| 4 | Evaluate p95 result | p95 response time **≤ 500ms** |
| 5 | Inspect error rate | Error rate is **0%** (no 5xx responses) during the load run |

### Expected Outcome
At 50 concurrent users, the login endpoint responds at p95 ≤ 500ms with no server errors.

---
